System Provisioning — profiles and combos

Author versioned FortiWeb system profiles (DNS, NTP, SNMP, administrators or any other config object), get them approved, preview and push them to selected appliances or the fleet, and group approved templates into zone × line × department combos.

What is it?#

System Provisioning pushes system-level configuration to FortiWeb appliances that already exist. You compose a system profile — an ordered list of configuration objects with the values to write — save it as a versioned template, have it approved, then preview it and push it to selected appliances or to the whole fleet with a canary first.

The same area holds Combos (called baselines in links and URLs): one combo per zone × line × department permutation, each carrying approved templates and applying them to the appliances classified into that scope.

To build a machine that does not exist yet, use Device Provisioning.

What does it do?#

  • Profiles: author, edit (each save is a new version), approve or reject, delete, and Preview & deploy an approved profile.
  • Element picker offers every FortiWeb configuration (cmdb) object known to the endpoint registry, grouped by GUI section, plus a curated set of system elements (global settings / hostname, DNS, NTP, FortiGuard, interfaces, static routes, SNMP, RADIUS, LDAP, user groups, admin access profiles, administrators, syslog, FortiAnalyzer).
  • Secret hygiene: secret-looking fields (passwords, shared secrets, keys) are removed from sensitive elements before the profile is saved, and are not pushed by a deployment. The deploy preview names the elements that go out without their secrets; set those on each device afterwards.
  • Two-phase apply: a dry-run preview of every request per appliance, then a confirmed, canary-gated live write.
  • Combos: generate the missing zone × line × department permutations, assign approved templates, see matching appliances, and roll a combo out as a background job.
  1. 1New profileelements + JSON values, optional scope
  2. 2Savestored as a pending template version
  3. 3Approveadmin approves (or rejects with a reason)
  4. 4Preview & deployHostname, Change ID, target appliances
  5. 5Previewdry-run requests per appliance
  6. 6Confirm & applycanary appliance first, then the rest

Requirements#

  • The FortiWeb ADOM. System Provisioning composes FortiWeb objects only; the menu entry is shown only in the FortiWeb ADOM, and the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs redirect to their home page if the URL is opened there. Opening it from the Global ADOM switches that tab to the FortiWeb ADOM.
  • The endpoint registry must be loaded, otherwise the element picker is empty ("No configuration objects are available from the registry yet. Load the registry / connect an appliance, then reload this page.").
  • Registered FortiWeb appliances to apply to.
  • For combos and profile scopes: zones, lines and departments defined in Classification, and appliances classified with them.

Permissions#

Every route requires the coarse config_write permission, except Approve and Reject, which require operations.template_approve.

Action Gate in code Granular key that is meant
Open profiles and combos, create/edit/delete a profile config_write operations.template_save
Preview & deploy a profile, apply a combo config_write operations.template_apply (one appliance), operations.apply (fleet)
Generate combos, assign/unassign templates config_write operations.template_save
Approve / Reject a profile operations.template_approve operations.template_approve (administrators only)
  • config_write is unlocked by any of operations.apply, operations.template_save, operations.template_apply, operations.template_approve, protection.edit, protection.apply, network.edit, network.apply, appliances.edit or appliances.apply. The coarse gate is therefore broader than the keys listed above: a profile holding only protection.edit can also deploy system profiles.
  • Without config_write the Automation menu group is not drawn and the pages answer 403 Forbidden. Viewer has no access; Operator can author and deploy; Administrator can also approve.
  • The Approve and Reject buttons are only shown, on Pending profiles, to users with operations.template_approve.
  • A live deploy needs an Approved profile regardless of who sends it: the server refuses a live apply of a pending or rejected version (the dry-run preview stays available).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Entire fleet and combo apply write only to the appliances visible to you in the current ADOM; before, they could reach every appliance in the database. A live deploy is refused unless the profile version is approved, Approve/Reject are only shown to approvers, and combos now push the system profiles assigned to them.

How to use#

Create a system profile#

  1. Open Automation → System Provisioning in the FortiWeb ADOM.
  2. Click New profile.
  3. Enter a Name.
  4. Optional: choose a Zone, Line and Department. Leaving one on — Any … — means the profile is not restricted on that facet.
  5. Under Provisioning elements, for each row: - Element: pick a configuration object. Objects marked (secret) carry secret material. - Singleton: ticked automatically for objects written as a whole (PUT without a key). Leave it unticked for collections. - mkey (optional): for a collection, the key of an existing object to update. Empty creates a new object. - Values: the fields to write, as a JSON object, e.g. { "hostname": "fweb-01" }.
  6. Use Add element, Move up, Move down and Remove element to shape the list. Elements are pushed in the order shown.
  7. Click Save profile. The list shows System profile "" saved (v1). and the profile with status Pending.

Edit a profile#

  1. Click Edit (pencil) on the profile.
  2. Change the elements or scope and click Save profile.

Saving always creates a new version (v2, v3 …) with status Pending; the previous version is kept. Saving under a different name creates a separate profile at v1. The list shows only the newest version of each profile.

Approve or reject#

An administrator with operations.template_approve:

  1. Clicks Approve (check mark) on a Pending profile — Approved "" v — now selectable for baselines., or
  2. Clicks Reject (cross), optionally types a Reason, and clicks Reject — Rejected "" v.

Only an Approved profile shows Preview & deploy.

Preview and deploy a profile#

  1. Click Preview & deploy (rocket) on an approved profile. The Deploy: dialog opens.
  2. Enter Hostname (the target device hostname for this deployment) and Change ID (e.g. CHG-0042). Both are required and are written to the audit log; neither is written to the appliance.
  3. Under Target, choose Selected appliances and pick one or more in Appliances, or choose Entire fleet (all appliances). Entire fleet means every appliance visible to you in this ADOM (maintenance devices only with appliances.view_maintenance), not every appliance in the database.
  4. Click Preview. The preview page lists, per appliance, every request (Method, Path, Body) that would be sent, with the profile's {{ variables }} already filled in with that appliance's values (see Per-device variables). Nothing has been written. When the profile holds elements whose secrets were stripped on save, a box Secrets are not part of this deployment. names them: they are pushed without their passwords and shared secrets.
  5. Click Confirm & apply to live devices and confirm the prompt.
  6. The result page shows Canary (the first appliance, written alone) and Remaining devices. If the canary fails: "Aborted. The canary device failed — the remaining devices were skipped."

On each appliance the requests run in order and stop at the first failed request; already-written requests on that appliance are not undone.

After the deployment, set the stripped passwords and shared secrets on each device (on the device itself or with a tool that sends them).

Per-device variables#

A profile may carry {{ name }} placeholders for values that differ per appliance (an address, a host name). Each appliance gets its own values from its binding to the profile, set in the Template Library under Devices this template governs (Variables (JSON), for example {"ntp_server": "192.0.2.123"}).

  • The preview and the live deploy render every request per appliance from that appliance's binding, as the Template Library's Apply does.
  • An appliance whose binding leaves a variable unset is named in the preview: The live deploy will be refused: fweb-02: no value for ntp_server. Set the values on the device bindings first.
  • The live deploy is then refused before anything is sent, canary included, with the appliance and the variable named. There is no override: set the value on the binding first.
  • A profile without placeholders is pushed the same to every appliance.

Work with combos#

  1. On System Provisioning, click Baselines. The Combos page opens.
  2. Click Generate missing combos (it pulses and shows a count when permutations are missing). One combo is created per zone × line × department permutation from Classification. Use it again after adding zones, lines or departments.
  3. Optional: filter by Zone, Line, Department or Search name, tick Save to my profile to remember the filter, and click Filter. Clear resets and forgets it. A combo whose facet is Any matches every filter value for that facet.
  4. Each card shows the combo scope, the number of Assigned templates and the number of Matching devices. Click a card to open the combo.

Assign templates from the combo page

  1. In Available to assign (latest version only), click Assign (+) next to an approved, scope-compatible system profile — Template assigned to combo.
  2. In Assigned templates, click Remove (×) and confirm — Template removed from combo.

Assign one template to many combos

  1. Under Approved templates on the Combos page, click Assign on a template. Click the eye button to View template content first if needed.
  2. In Assign to combos — , tick the combos it should belong to (filter with Zone / Line / Department, Select all, Clear all). Unticking removes it from that combo.
  3. Click Save assignments — Updated combo assignments (+ / -).

Apply a combo

  1. On the combo page, click Apply to device(s)… (shown only when the combo has assigned templates and matching appliances).
  2. Review the dry-run preview and the Matching devices list. Only matching appliances visible to you in the current ADOM are targeted.
  3. Click Confirm live apply (canary-gated) and confirm. The rollout starts as a background job: Baseline rollout "" started for device(s) — progress appears in the job dock (bottom right).

A combo push writes every assigned template in combo order: endpoint templates (such as those from the Template Library) and system profiles alike. A system profile contributes the same requests as its Preview & deploy, element by element, without its stripped secrets.

{{ variables }} are rendered per device in a combo too, and each assigned template takes the variables of its own binding on that device. The preview names every device left without a value (The live rollout will be refused: …), and the confirmed rollout is then refused before it starts, with the devices and variables named; there is no override.

Configuration#

Profile

Field Description Required Example
Name Profile name; versions are counted per name. Yes fortiweb-baseline
Zone / Line / Department Optional scope from Classification. Used to offer the profile to compatible combos. No DMZ
Element Configuration object to write. At least one row DNS
mkey Key of an existing collection object to update. No port1
Singleton Write the whole object without a key. No ticked for DNS
Values JSON object with the fields to write. No (defaults to {}) {"hostname": "fweb-01"}

Deploy dialog

Field Description Required Example
Hostname Target hostname, recorded in the flash message and the audit log. Yes fweb-01.example.com
Change ID Change reference, recorded in the flash message and the audit log. Yes CHG-0042
Target Selected appliances or Entire fleet (all appliances). Yes Selected appliances
Appliances Appliances visible in this ADOM (Ctrl/Cmd-click for several). Ignored for Entire fleet. For Selected fweb-01

How an element becomes a request:

Element settings Request
Singleton ticked Update the whole object (no key)
Not singleton, mkey set Update the object with that key
Not singleton, mkey empty Create a new object

Values are wrapped in the {"data": …} envelope FortiWeb expects, and server-managed fields are removed before sending.

Example#

🧪Example — Push DNS and SNMP settings to two appliances

  1. New profile site-base. Elements: - DNS, Singleton, Values with the DNS fields to write. - SNMP (sysinfo), Singleton, Values with the SNMP system fields to write.
  2. Save profile → System profile "site-base" saved (v1).
  3. An administrator clicks Approve.
  4. Preview & deploy: Hostname fweb-01.example.com, Change ID CHG-0042, Selected appliances fweb-01 and fweb-02, Preview.
  5. Check the two update requests listed for each appliance, then Confirm & apply to live devices.
  6. The canary appliance is written first; the other follows only if the canary succeeded.

Result#

  • Audit log entries: provisioning.save, provisioning.preview, provisioning.apply, provisioning.delete, provisioning.approve, provisioning.reject; for combos baseline.generate, baseline.assign, baseline.unassign, baseline.template_combos, baseline.apply.preview, baseline.apply.start and, when the job ends, baseline.apply. See Audit log.
  • Each live write records the object's previous state in the change history before writing.
  • A combo rollout is a job that can be stopped; it stops between requests, never in the middle of one. It ends as Applied to x/y device(s), Aborted — canary device failed (x/y ok), Completed with failures — x/y device(s) ok or Stopped — ….
  • A profile deploy that takes longer than the inline window also continues as a job.

Troubleshooting#

"Could not save profile: Profile name is required"#

Possible causes - Name was empty.

Solution 1. Enter a name and click Save profile. Your rows are kept on the form.

Verification - The profile appears in the list as Pending.

"Could not save profile: Add at least one provisioning element"#

Possible causes - Every row has Element left on — select a configuration object —.

Solution 1. Pick an element in at least one row.

Verification - System profile "" saved (v).

"Could not save profile: Element '

Possible causes - The Values box is not valid JSON (missing quotes, trailing comma). - A similar message "values must be a JSON object" means the JSON is a list or a single value.

Solution 1. Correct the JSON so it is one object: { "field": "value" }.

Verification - The profile saves.

"Could not save profile: Unknown provisioning element: "#

Possible causes - The element no longer exists in the endpoint registry (shown in the picker as (not in registry)).

Solution 1. Choose another element or remove the row.

Verification - The profile saves.

Preview & deploy is not offered#

Possible causes - The newest version is Pending or Rejected. Editing an approved profile creates a new pending version.

Solution 1. Have an administrator approve the newest version.

Verification - The rocket button appears on the row.

"Hostname and Change ID are required."#

Possible causes - One of the two fields was empty.

Solution 1. Open Preview & deploy again and fill in both.

Verification - The preview page opens.

"Select at least one appliance, or choose "Entire fleet"."#

Possible causes - Selected appliances was chosen with nothing selected. SATOM refuses rather than treating an empty selection as the fleet.

Solution 1. Select appliances, or choose Entire fleet (all appliances) explicitly.

Verification - The preview lists the intended appliances.

"Aborted. The canary device failed — the remaining devices were skipped."#

Possible causes - A request failed on the first appliance; the failing row shows the error.

Solution 1. Fix the profile values (or the appliance), save, get the new version approved, and deploy again.

Verification - The canary block shows OK.

A secret field was not written#

Possible causes - Saving removes secret-looking fields from sensitive elements, and a deployment does not send them. The preview names the affected elements.

Solution 1. Set the secret on the appliance directly, or through a tool that sends it.

Verification - Check the object on the appliance.

"… is pending: only an approved system profile can be deployed live."#

Possible causes - Confirm & apply to live devices was sent for a version that is Pending or Rejected (for example a preview opened before a new version was saved). The refusal is recorded in the audit log; nothing was written.

Solution 1. Have an administrator approve the version, then deploy again.

Verification - The result page shows the Canary block.

"Profile not found or locked."#

Possible causes - The template is locked (its delete button is disabled) or was already deleted.

Solution 1. A locked profile (lock icon next to its name) cannot be deleted from this page. Reload the list to check whether it was already removed.

Verification - The row is gone, or shows the lock icon.

"Deploy of "" refused — : no value for . Set the values on the device bindings, then apply."#

The same cause shows on a combo as Baseline rollout "<name>" refused — ….

Possible causes - The profile (or a template of the combo) has a {{ variable }} placeholder, and the named device's binding gives it no value.

Solution 1. Open the template in the Template Library and, under Devices this template governs, set the variable in the device's Variables (JSON). 2. Preview again.

Verification - The preview no longer shows The live deploy will be refused: ….

"Baseline "" matches no devices for its scope."#

Possible causes - No appliance has the combo's zone, line and department.

Solution 1. Classify appliances (see Classification).

Verification - The combo card shows a non-zero Matching devices count.

"Baseline "" has no composing templates."#

Possible causes - Nothing is assigned to the combo, or the assigned templates contain no elements.

Solution 1. Assign the templates to push via Assign on the combo page or the Combos page.

Verification - The apply preview lists requests.

"All combos already exist — nothing to generate."#

Possible causes - Every permutation already has a combo.

Solution 1. Add zones, lines or departments in Classification first if you expected new combos.

Verification - Generate missing combos shows a count.

"Could not assign: Template "" is not approved"#

Possible causes - The template is pending or rejected.

Solution 1. Approve it, then assign again.

Verification - Template assigned to combo.

Advanced#

Advanced How profiles are stored
  • A profile is a template of kind system-profile with a body of line, _scope (zone, line, department) and items (key, endpoint, data, singleton, mkey, label, sensitive).
  • An element is sensitive when the curated catalog says so (SNMP v3 users, RADIUS, LDAP, administrators) or its name contains words such as password, secret, radius, ldap, admin. For sensitive elements, any field whose name contains password, passwd, pwd, secret, psk, passphrase, private-key, privkey or credential is removed recursively before saving.
  • Approval is per version: approving v3 does not approve v4.
Advanced Apply mechanics
  • The canary is one appliance. After it succeeds, the remaining appliances are written in parallel (up to 8 at a time).
  • Entire fleet sends the runner the explicit list of appliances visible to you in this ADOM, the same set the preview header counts. An empty device list never means "every appliance".
  • The approval status is checked by the server at the live write, not only by hiding the button: a pending or rejected version gets its dry-run preview but never a live apply. The refusal is audited as provisioning.apply.
Advanced Combos
  • Combo names are built as Zone / Line / Department, with Any for an empty facet. When a classification list is empty it contributes a single Any slot; the all-Any combination is not created.
  • Matching appliances are those whose zone, line and department equal the combo's non-empty facets. The match is not limited to FortiWeb appliances, but an apply targets only the matching appliances visible to you in the current ADOM.
  • The combo page offers only approved system-profile templates compatible with the combo scope; the Assign to combos dialog on the Combos page accepts any approved template of the ADOM.
  • The saved filter is stored per user under the setting baselines.filters.
  • A form to create or edit a combo by hand exists at /web/provisioning/baselines/new and /web/provisioning/baselines/<id>/edit (name, zone, line, department, approved system profiles, note); no menu or button links to it.
